title: Foundation Door Genealogy — Seeds of Death, Seeds of Life, Time and Place
status: cross-domain Foundation genealogy derived from canonical Foundation records plus verified geographic anchors
purpose: Show how every current Foundation record approaches, crosses, rises from, falls back toward, or is refounded through the Door by pairing project-native Seed states with concrete historical clocks and physical/institutional places.
master_rule: Do not call a whole religion, institution, nation, company, movement or school a Seed of Death or Seed of Life. The terms describe states in a Foundation transition: prior form/rupture/compression on one side of the Door and viable reproducible capacity on the other.

door_model.pre_door: Seed of Death / compressed predecessor / rupture / insufficiency / loss / unresolved problem / completed predecessor role.
door_model.threshold: Door crossing: signature, migration, vow, declaration, charter, incorporation, protocol switch, merger, first school/community, publication or another event that changes what can operate.
door_model.post_door: Seed of Life: a viable rule/practice/text/institution/protocol/community that can be repeated by people other than the originator.
door_model.rise: Seed of Life → first operation → reproduction → branching → Fruit.
door_model.fall: A Foundation can fall by closure, capture, merger, supersession, diaspora, loss of reproduction, terminal dormancy or forced dissolution.
door_model.return: Fall does not always equal annihilation. A closed institution can leave transferable Seed in text, trained people, protocols, diaspora communities or successor institutions.
door_model.refoundation: When residue crosses the Door again under revised rules, the lineage may be refounded rather than restarted from zero.

place_model.rule: A Foundation may have several places because proposal, signature, legal force, first operation, migration and refoundation can occur in different locations.
place_model.precision_rule: Never invent an exact building when only a city, region, country or distributed network is established.

emergent_patterns.finding: Most mature Foundations have multiple births rather than one birthday.
emergent_patterns.evidence: Across the atlas, proposal/seed, signature/authorization, entry into force, first operation, consolidation and refoundation frequently occur on different dates.

emergent_patterns.finding: The Door is often materially embodied as a move, signature, room, building, incorporation, migration or protocol cutover.
The death-side is frequently not literal death but the moment an old operating form becomes insufficient, is destroyed, is completed, or must be surrendered.
When a physical center is destroyed or closed, the surviving Foundation often becomes more portable if its rules, texts, training or community memory can travel.

The life-side is best detected by reproduction: later people can perform the practice, instantiate the protocol, teach the method, govern the institution or branch the lineage without the founder being physically present.
The strongest empirical test of a Foundation is what survives when the original person, building, technology, regime or generation disappears.
emergent_patterns.test: If nothing transferable survives, there was an event or project but not yet a durable Foundation.

emergent_patterns.finding: Foundations often migrate geographically while preserving a recognizable rule set.
A refoundation is structurally a second Door crossing: residue from the previous form is selectively preserved, discarded or recombined into a new operating platform.
